pr_body:
Fixes #43020 when a thread uses ClassDB while main thread calls is_parent_class().

I cannot test that this fixes the issue, because it is not easily reproducible currently.

issue_context.title: ClassDB: Improper use of RWLock: Deadlock when updating resource previews
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
master: 32be9299ba177781d22bffa8e7e848fcca33b860
3.2: 2e073ecbeaf5b502c2b8c3c0510e4a22a56db58f

**OS/device including version:**
Windows 10 [10.0.18362.1082]
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti
Driver 452.06

**Issue description:**
My project randomly hangs (deadlocks) while opening.

Investigating with the debugger and reading the code, I found some re-entrant usage of OBJTYPE_RLOCK macro (RWLock::read_lock).

```cpp
bool ClassDB::is_parent_class(const StringName &p_class, const StringName &p_inherits) {

	OBJTYPE_RLOCK;

	StringName inherits = p_class;

	while (inherits.operator String().length()) {

		if (inherits == p_inherits)
			return true;
		inherits = get_parent_class(inherits);
	}

	return false;
}

...

StringName ClassDB::get_parent_class(const StringName &p_class) {

	OBJTYPE_RLOCK;

	ClassInfo *ti = classes.getptr(p_class);
	ERR_FAIL_COND_V_MSG(!ti, StringName(), "Cannot get class '" + String(p_class) + "'.");
	return ti->inherits;
}
```

From some cursory look at the MSDN documentation at https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sync/slim-reader-writer--srw--locks , they make an explicit note that Exclusive access cannot be done re-entrantly, but misleadingly, no note is made about re-entrant Shared access.

However, it does make this comment: "There is no guarantee about the order in which threads that request ownership will be granted ownership; SRW locks are neither fair nor FIFO."

This could imply that re-entrant usage of shared locking is unspecified behavior. Based on debugger stacktraces, this is the only explanation I can come up with.

Additionally, I browsed a ReactOS reference implementation available at https://doxygen.reactos.org/d1/db8/srw_8c_source.html , which shows that if the main thread ever attempts to call `RtlAcquireSRWLockExclusive`, then the `RTL_SRWLOCK_CONTENDED` flag will be set on the RWLock, and any further attempts to call `RtlAcquireSRWLockShared`, even by the re-entrant thread, will wait.

I think this is evidence that it is not safe to call `RtlAcquireSRWLockShared`, and by `OBJTYPE_RLOCK` in a nested way within a single thread.

To fix this, I suspect a few functions may have to be refactored in ClassDB, and we should verify the implementations of ResourceCache, ObjectDB, AnimatedTexture (in Godot 3.2), and any similar usages of RWLock in Godot master.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Get a bunch of assets into your project. What I did was I downloaded a bunch of .vrm (glTF) models (about 15 of them) from VRoidHub and renamed them to .glb
2. open and close the project a bunch.
3. Randomly, the editor will hang on project load. It happened two times to me today, but never before today.

comments:
Also linked to #42213: This comment makes it sound related: "FYI disabling the thumbnail editor feature as described in #42785, also fixed for me your project."

That does sound a lot like "EditorResourcePreview" being responsible.

Regarding #42785, however, there might be more going on... I suspect some comments are people who read "Godot hangs when opening project", but instead have this issue.

The stacktrace posted by @akien-mga at https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/42785#issuecomment-710118787 does not look like this issue, so it's unclear... but also Remi is on Linux, while I was on Windows.

Did some reading through all code using RWLock (All code is roughly the same in both 3.2 and master).

Other than ClassDB, I think Godot uses RWLock properly, so this issue should focus only on ClassDB. (I'm ignoring proxy cycles in AnimatedTexture)

These are the three problematic interactions I found.
is_parent_class -> get_parent_class
get_inheriters_from_class -> is_parent_class
get_direct_inheriters_from_class -> get_parent_class

Some public functions do not acquire OBJTYPE_RLOCK. I do not understand the rules for which public functions lock, and which do not, so I will not touch these.

So to fix this bug, I propose adding two new functions to be called internally: _get_parent_class and _is_parent_class, which do not acquire OBJTYPE_RLOCK.
I will try to get to this soon.

review_comments: You kept `OBJTYPE_RLOCK;` in `_is_parent_class`, so aren't you locking twice? It seems to contradict the comment in the header.
Seems like you got it wrong in the `master` PR, but the `3.2` one is correct.
Wow good catch, merging is dangerous. Almost like the goto fail bug.
